title: Puss in Boots
summary: A sad young person gets a smart animal that asks for clothes and food.
coverScene: A clever cat wearing shiny black boots proudly walks down a country road.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a poor man died.
He left his young son nothing except a fast cat.
At first, the young son felt sad.
He thought this family gift was very small.
However, the smart animal looked at his master.
He asked for only two things.
He wanted a pair of fine black shoes and a bag to catch food.
The master gave him those items.
The cat put on the shoes at once.
Using good plans, the animal began bringing food gifts to the king.
He presented a nice animal and spoke a high name.
He always told the court that the gift came from his master, the Marquis of Carabas.
The king received the gift with joy.
Many people saw the kind gifts arriving at the great house.
The court officers wondered who the sender could be.
The cat felt proud of his work.
He planned to bring more food the next day.
The king wanted to meet the sender of these fine presents.
He sent a message to the court about the matter.
One day, the cat learned that the king would travel near the river with his daughter.
The fast cat told his master to swim in the water.
The cat hid the man clothes.
When the king transport arrived, the cat shouted.
He shouted that the rich man was down in the water.
The king at once sent guards to save the young man.
The king provided him with wonderful clothes.
The young man looked very good in the new clothes.
The king smiled at the marquis and asked him to join the ride.
While the king drove along the road, the cat ran ahead to manage a plan.
He commanded local workers in the fields.
He told them to tell the king that the land belonged to the marquis.
Workers told the king that the fields belonged to the marquis.
The king felt very interested because the supposed man owned such large properties.
The king looked around the fields with great interest.
He thanked the marquis for having such fine land.
Meanwhile, the cat entered a great house.
That house belonged to a powerful, rich strong man.
The dangerous owner could change his shape into any animal that he wanted.
The smart cat acted to feel doubt.
He asked if the strong man could become a tiny mouse.
The strong man changed into a small mouse.
The fast cat jumped on him.
He caught the little animal right away and won the fine house for his master.
The cat felt very happy about this success.
He waited for the king to arrive at the big house.
When the king arrived at the great house, the happy cat welcomed the guests outside.
Delighted by the lovely marquis and his vast lands, the king offered his daughter in marriage.
The young man married the lady and became a rich leader.
As for the fast animal, he lived happily.
He never needed to follow mice again except for his own fun.

sentences.text: Upon the melancholy dissolution of an impoverished miller, his estate proved meager indeed, leaving his youngest son nothing more than a seemingly unremarkable cat.
At first, the young man succumbed to a heavy sorrow, believing this solitary creature was a pitiful inheritance incapable of sustaining a livelihood.
However, the feline surveyed his despondent master with a remarkably astute gaze that suggested hidden depths of intellect.
Quietly, the animal requested only two provisions to alter their shared destiny: a sturdy pair of custom leather boots and a sack suited for gathering sustenance.
Though perplexed by these unusual demands, the master provided the items, and the cat laced the footwear with deliberate care.
Donning the boots immediately, the clever animal transformed himself into a dedicated provider through a series of calculated maneuvers.
He ventured into the dense surrounding woods, cunningly trapping plump game and presenting the offerings directly to the sovereign as tribute.
Whenever the animal delivered these fine specimens to the royal court, he announced them with a grand and fabricated title.
He insisted that every single offering originated from his wealthy and distinguished master, whom he named the Marquis of Carabas.
The king, delighted by the unexpected generosity, received each present with profound gratitude while the young master remained entirely unaware of his rising fame.
Throughout the realm, whispers began to circulate concerning the mysterious and generous aristocrat who showered the royal house with such exquisite gifts.
The cat labored tirelessly each day, meticulously constructing a powerful reputation for his master to ensure universal admiration.
He planted stories among the townsfolk, cultivating the illusion that the marquis possessed vast estates, magnificent manors, and immense wealth.
Curiosity plagued the king, who frequently questioned his ministers regarding the identity of this elusive nobleman whom nobody had ever directly encountered.
Hearing these discussions, the cat smiled with quiet satisfaction, knowing his intricate plan was unfolding with absolute precision.
One afternoon, the clever animal learned that the royal carriage would soon travel along the winding path beside the local river.
Acting swiftly, the cat instructed his bewildered master to enter the water and pretend he was drowning.
While the young man splashed near the riverbank, the faithful feline gathered his master's worn garments and concealed them beneath a large rock.
Just as the royal vehicle drew near, the cat began to cry out with feigned panic that the noble marquis was slipping beneath the surface.
Recognizing the esteemed title from the countless previous gifts, the king immediately commanded his guards to rescue the drowning man.
The royal guards pulled the master from the water with great haste, offering him dry shelter and garments crafted from the finest silks.
Draped in the magnificent attire provided by the sovereign, the young man suddenly possessed the distinguished appearance of a true aristocrat.
The king looked upon him with genuine warmth and invited the newly rescued marquis to join him inside the royal carriage for the remainder of the journey.
Overwhelmed by this sudden twist of fortune, the master accepted the invitation and sat comfortably beside the monarch.
As they conversed about various subjects, the king's daughter glanced sideways at the handsome stranger, smiling and finding him remarkably charming.
While the carriage rumbled along the dusty road, the ambitious cat raced ahead of the royal procession to execute the next phase of his grand design.
Encountering local peasants laboring furiously in the sun-drenched fields, the cat issued a stern warning concerning what would happen if they disobeyed.
He commanded them to inform the king that every acre of the surrounding land belonged exclusively to the Marquis of Carabas.
When the royal vehicle eventually passed, the king inquired of the workers whose property they tended, and they repeated the exact phrase the cat had taught them.
Deeply impressed by the sheer expanse of these prosperous lands, the monarch congratulated his traveling companion on possessing such a magnificent domain.
Meanwhile, the clever animal approached a towering stone fortress that belonged to an immensely wealthy and terrifying giant.
This formidable master of the castle possessed the rare and dark ability to transform his physical form into any creature he desired.
The cat requested an audience, entering the great hall with a calm demeanor despite the intimidating presence of the magical owner.
Feigning respectful doubt, the feline asked whether the giant could truly assume the shape of something as small as a common house mouse.
Boasting proudly, the foolish giant instantly vanished and reappeared as a tiny rodent scurrying across the stone floor.
The cat had anticipated this exact moment with calculated patience, watching the transformation unfold with predatory focus.
Moving with astonishing speed, the feline leaped forward before the tiny mouse could comprehend the trap closing around him.
He caught the creature instantly, ending the reign of the magical tyrant and securing the fortress for his master in a single decisive movement.
The giant vanished forever, leaving the magnificent castle entirely unoccupied and ready for a new lineage of nobility.
The victorious cat settled inside the grand hall, waiting peacefully for the arrival of the royal guests.
When the royal carriage finally rolled through the heavy iron gates, the clever animal stood proudly on the stone steps to welcome them.
Bowing deeply, he announced the arrival of the estate in the name of his illustrious master, the Marquis of Carabas.
Completely enchanted by the sprawling lands, the magnificent fortress, and the charming nobleman, the king made a generous proposal.
He offered the hand of his beloved daughter in marriage to the young man, securing a royal future for the former miller's son.
The wedding celebration that followed lasted for many days, drawing cheerful crowds from every corner of the prosperous kingdom.
The newly wedded couple lived in absolute splendor, while the former poor man finally understood the full value of his unusual inheritance.
As for the faithful cat, he retired from his scheming ways, lounging comfortably by the hearth in the great hall whenever he desired warmth.
He occasionally chased a mouse across the stone floor, though purely for his own amusement rather than out of any desperate necessity.
The king showered the household with generous gifts, ensuring that peace and prosperity reigned over the region for decades to come.
Long after the celebrations faded into memory, the tale of the clever feline and his master lived on as the most celebrated story in the land.
